summary: Licona defended resurrection through historical and comparative inference; Dillahunty more effectively separated reported events, unexplained anomalies, supernatural classification, and justified causal attribution.

pro.text: these experiences occurred in individual and in group
pro.context: Licona presented early Pauline testimony and apostolic contact as historical support for individual and group appearance experiences.

con.text: I will not accept the explanation
con.context: Dillahunty distinguished accepting that an extraordinary event occurred from accepting an unsupported supernatural causal account.

pro-background-cumulative-paranormal-evi.words: Several independently reported paranormal phenomena collectively suggest that reality may include a supernatural dimension, supplying background plausibility for resurrection.
pro-background-cumulative-paranormal-evi.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers a coherent cumulative-evidence strategy, explicitly presents supernaturalism as an empirically suggestive background proposition, and connects several announced experience categories to the debate's subsidiary plausibility burden. Principal limitation: The selected evidence only announces those categories, leaving supernatural dimension partly undefined and providing neither case verification nor disciplined comparison with psychological, testimonial, fraudulent, or presently unknown natural explanations. Live burden: The affirmative still must demonstrate that independently reliable cases survive ordinary causal screening and that their combined evidential force supports a supernatural ontology rather than merely a heterogeneous collection of unresolved anomalies. Locked score: The mixed band reflects substantial relevance and intelligible cumulative structure alongside materially overstated calibration, compressed inferential bridging, and comparatively underdeveloped evidential substantiation.

pro-historical-pauline-apostolic-bedrock.words: Paul's early testimony, claimed experience, apostolic contacts, and shared proclamation support historical claims of individual, hostile, and group resurrection appearances.
pro-historical-pauline-apostolic-bedrock.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies an early source, connects Paul with Jesus's disciples, and constructs a historically significant evidential foundation encompassing individual, hostile, and group appearance traditions central to the affirmative case. Principal limitation: Its virtually-undisputed framing compresses important distinctions among reported belief, subjective experience, transmitted proclamation, and veridical appearance, while the breadth of scholarly agreement and independence of corroboration remain insufficiently qualified. Live burden: The affirmative must establish precisely what the earliest sources warrant, how independently the traditions support one another, and why their evidential accessibility and reliability justify treating the asserted experiences as historical data requiring explanation. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects excellent burden relevance, clear source-based organization, and meaningful historical warrant, moderated by scope instability and somewhat overstated evidential conclusions.

pro-comparative-ibt-explanatory-criteria.words: Using explanatory scope, power, plausibility, and limited ad hocness, resurrection allegedly explains Paul and reported group appearances better than hallucination.
pro-comparative-ibt-explanatory-criteria.critique: Strongest feature: The move uses recognizable inference-to-best-explanation criteria, grants hallucination meaningful scope and economy, and directly compares its expected consequences with Paul and the asserted group appearances. Principal limitation: The treatment narrows hallucination to insufficiently developed variants, assumes contested historical data, and omits fuller consideration of priors, alternative psychological models, mixed explanations, transmission error, and other naturalistic possibilities. Live burden: The affirmative must compare strengthened rival hypotheses under the same criteria, defend the reliability of every fact being explained, and show that resurrection contributes discriminating explanatory content rather than benefiting chiefly from weaknesses assigned to competitors. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects central relevance and genuine comparative reasoning, tempered by underdeveloped rival modeling, limited representational charity, and slightly overstated confidence.

con-evidential-default-and-burden.words: Resurrection proponents must overcome evidential withholding by showing their hypothesis superior, rather than expecting skepticism or the practical default to be disproved.
con-evidential-default-and-burden.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly places the affirmative evidential burden on resurrection proponents and establishes a motion-level reason for withholding belief until comparative superiority receives adequate support. Principal limitation: Its null-hypothesis terminology shifts among practical default, assumed truth, unconfirmed proposition, and criminal-law analogy, risking the stronger claim that skepticism is true rather than simply evidentially appropriate. Live burden: The skeptical case must formulate withholding without reifying a null position and must examine whether the particular Pauline, apostolic, and appearance evidence actually satisfies or fails the proposed evidential threshold. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects exceptional motion relevance, coherent burden allocation, and useful calibration of assent, reduced by conceptual instability and only partial engagement with the affirmative's concrete historical premises and explanatory criteria.

con-anomalies-do-not-establish-supernatu.words: Unexplained experiences cannot establish a supernatural realm while that category remains negatively defined, unconfirmed, and unsupported by discriminating causal investigation.
con-anomalies-do-not-establish-supernatu.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely distinguishes reports attributed to supernatural causes from confirmation of a supernatural realm, directly diagnosing the central inferential gap in the affirmative's cumulative background case. Principal limitation: It remains chiefly methodological and does not inspect representative paranormal cases, their safeguards, or the possibility that independently robust anomaly classes could acquire cumulative evidential force without individually establishing supernaturalism. Live burden: The skeptical side must show how ordinary causal screening applies to the strongest announced examples while preserving its appropriately limited conclusion that unexplained does not mean false, fraudulent, or necessarily natural. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent responsiveness, stable terminology, matched calibration, and coherent causal caution, with some evidential limitation because the displayed reply challenges the inference more thoroughly than the underlying cases.

con-resurrection-lacks-explanatory-conte.words: Eliminating hoax or lacking a satisfactory natural account does not establish resurrection when divine action supplies no discriminating mechanism or explanatory content.
con-resurrection-lacks-explanatory-conte.critique: Strongest feature: The move clearly separates defeating a rival explanation from positively supporting resurrection and directly challenges whether divine action contributes testable, discriminating, or causally informative explanatory content. Principal limitation: Equating every divine explanation with magic overstates the criticism because intentional-agent explanations can sometimes explain without specifying a physical mechanism, provided independent evidence identifies the agent, capability, and relevant intention. Live burden: The skeptical case must specify what positive content a minimally adequate resurrection hypothesis would require and why the affirmative's historical, theological, and comparative considerations fail to supply that content. Locked score: The very strong band reflects direct contact with the central comparative bridge, excellent diagnostic responsiveness, and substantial evidential warrant, moderated by a somewhat categorical dismissal that understates possible agent-level explanations.

con-divine-agent-requires-prior-support.words: Resurrection becomes plausible only with grounds for a capable and willing divine agent; generic supernaturalism and private revelation do not independently provide them.
con-divine-agent-requires-prior-support.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies a genuine missing component in the affirmative hypothesis by distinguishing generic supernatural background evidence from evidence for an agent capable of and disposed toward raising Jesus. Principal limitation: Describing prior belief in such an agent as necessary confuses antecedent plausibility with an absolute prerequisite and neglects the possibility that sufficiently discriminating event evidence could update the probability of divine agency. Live burden: The skeptical side must restate the objection probabilistically, explain what evidence would distinguish a purposeful divine act from unknown alternatives, and assess whether the resurrection evidence itself supplies any such discrimination. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects substantial relevance and a coherent background-probability challenge, constrained by materially overstated necessity, incomplete qualification, and an unsupported bridge from needing agent content to requiring prior belief.

con-no-workable-supernatural-causal-meth.words: Science and history cannot confirm supernatural causation without a positive definition and a method distinguishing that cause from error, fraud, hallucination, or unknown nature.
con-no-workable-supernatural-causal-meth.critique: Strongest feature: The move sharply distinguishes investigating events attributed to supernatural causes from confirming a supernatural causal connection and identifies causal discrimination as the decisive methodological requirement. Principal limitation: Saying inquiry is barred until supernatural ontology is positively understood may demand more than causal investigation ordinarily requires, since hypotheses can sometimes be tested through predicted contrasts before their underlying ontology is comprehensively explained. Live burden: The skeptical case must articulate workable minimum criteria for supernatural attribution and demonstrate that resurrection evidence fails those criteria without treating every nonnatural hypothesis as methodologically inadmissible by definition. Locked score: The very strong band reflects central burden contact, precise event-cause separation, outstanding diagnostic responsiveness, and strong methodological coherence, tempered only by a somewhat excessive prerequisite concerning complete positive understanding of supernatural causation.

pro-methods-discipline-specific-investig.words: Historical and scientific disciplines employ different methods, so absence of controlled repeatability alone does not disqualify alleged supernatural events from responsible investigation.
pro-methods-discipline-specific-investig.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly observes that disciplines employ different investigative methods and usefully rejects controlled laboratory repeatability as a universal prerequisite for examining singular historical or allegedly paranormal events. Principal limitation: Methodological diversity establishes admissibility for investigation, not a successful causal inference, and the announced examples remain insufficiently connected to standards capable of distinguishing supernatural action from testimony error, fraud, coincidence, psychology, or unknown natural processes. Live burden: The affirmative must specify discipline-appropriate verification and causal-discrimination procedures, then show that the cited phenomena and resurrection traditions satisfy them rather than merely falling outside repeatable experimentation. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects clear methodological precision, apt qualification, and direct engagement with exclusion concerns, reduced because the response only partially answers the stronger demand for warranted supernatural attribution.

pro-causation-against-methodological-exc.words: Automatically preferring any natural explanation can prejudge anomalous evidence and prevent recognition of events that known natural causes cannot plausibly explain.
pro-causation-against-methodological-exc.critique: Strongest feature: The private-information hypothetical effectively demonstrates how automatic preference for any natural explanation could prejudge evidence and clarifies the affirmative's concern about methodological exclusion rather than ordinary evidential caution. Principal limitation: Showing that dogmatic exclusion would be defective does not establish a supernatural cause, distinguish one from unknown natural alternatives, or demonstrate that ancient resurrection evidence possesses the hypothetical's immediacy, specificity, and independently checkable informational strength. Live burden: The affirmative must provide a noncircular threshold for concluding that known natural explanations are genuinely inadequate and explain what positive features license supernatural classification after that threshold is crossed. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a coherent, relevant challenge to prior exclusion and a vivid counterexample, moderated by incomplete causal discrimination and limited transfer from the hypothetical to the historical case.

pro-comparative-case-by-case-resurrectio.words: Historical hypotheses should be compared case by case against known data and relevant background evidence, with resurrection allegedly outperforming every naturalistic alternative.
pro-comparative-case-by-case-resurrectio.critique: Strongest feature: The move endorses disciplined case-by-case comparison using known historical data and directly addresses the affirmative's central obligation to establish resurrection as the comparatively preferable explanation. Principal limitation: The categorical claim that resurrection wins every comparison exceeds the displayed support because only hallucination is substantially mentioned, while the completeness of the rival set, historical dataset, background assumptions, and probability judgments remains undefended. Live burden: The affirmative must present strengthened versions of the principal naturalistic and mixed hypotheses, apply identical explanatory criteria transparently, and show why resurrection's positive content outweighs its demanding prior commitments. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct central relevance and an appropriate comparative framework, constrained by compressed analysis, incomplete rival coverage, and calibration that reaches beyond the evidence actually presented in the selected exchange.

con-test-before-supernatural-attribution.words: Methodological naturalism permits testing extraordinary events while withholding supernatural attribution until evidence distinguishes the phenomenon from fraud, error, hallucination, and natural alternatives.
con-test-before-supernatural-attribution.critique: Strongest feature: The reply clearly distinguishes permission to test an extraordinary event from permission to attribute it supernaturally, directly answering the claim that methodological naturalism prevents investigation from beginning. Principal limitation: The formulation says little about what evidence could confirm supernatural causation, potentially leaving attribution indefinitely postponed even when an event generated highly specific contrasts against fraud, error, hallucination, and known natural alternatives. Live burden: The skeptical side must identify a principled evidential threshold for causal attribution and explain why the affirmative's historical and paranormal evidence falls below it without converting methodological caution into prior exclusion. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise scope, matched calibration, exceptional responsiveness, and a powerful clarification of investigative practice, with a limited residual burden to make the proposed test-and-confirm standard operational rather than merely restrictive.

con-paul-and-reports-insufficient.words: Paul offers limited direct access to Jesus's life, death, burial, and tomb, while surviving reports do not independently demonstrate a physical return from death.
con-paul-and-reports-insufficient.critique: Strongest feature: The reply grants Paul's importance while precisely identifying his lack of direct access to Jesus's ministry, execution, burial, and empty-tomb history, thereby challenging the affirmative's central historical foundation. Principal limitation: Direct eyewitness access to every underlying event is not required for all historical knowledge, and the selected criticism does not fully evaluate Paul's claimed experience, apostolic contacts, early tradition, or possible corroboration from other sources. Live burden: The skeptical side must assess the complete transmission chain, independence, dating, and content of the appearance traditions and show why their combined warrant remains insufficient despite Paul's proximity to principal witnesses. Locked score: The very strong band reflects focused source criticism, careful calibration, substantial relevance, and direct responsiveness, moderated by the need for fuller engagement with indirect historical corroboration and testimonial convergence.

con-supernatural-label-does-not-identify.words: Calling an unexplained event supernatural merely labels current explanatory absence and cannot identify gods, spirits, souls, resurrection, or another particular cause.
con-supernatural-label-does-not-identify.critique: Strongest feature: The move consistently separates absence of a presently accepted natural account from positive identification of a supernatural cause and directly challenges the affirmative's repeated movement between anomaly and explanation. Principal limitation: The criticism risks treating every supernatural classification as merely verbal, although a carefully defined hypothesis might acquire evidential support from distinctive predictions even without identifying a complete mechanism or particular agent. Live burden: The skeptical side must explain which discriminating observations would move an event beyond unexplained status and show that the resurrection case lacks those observations rather than assuming causal underdetermination permanently. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent precision, appropriate calibration, strong central relevance, and highly responsive diagnosis of the inferential gap, while leaving a modest obligation to specify positive standards for causal identification.

con-five-hundred-claim-uninvestigable.words: The reported appearance to five hundred lacks accessible identities, individual statements, and described experiences needed to investigate whether the event occurred as claimed.
con-five-hundred-claim-uninvestigable.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly shifts attention from explaining a supposed mass experience to first establishing an investigable event through accessible identities, statements, circumstances, and independently assessable testimony. Principal limitation: Present inability to interview named witnesses does not make every ancient group report evidentially worthless, and the reply does not examine whether the report's early transmission, public framing, or relation to other traditions provides limited indirect support. Live burden: The skeptical side must distinguish weak historical evidence from no evidence and explain why the surviving report lacks sufficient specificity, corroboration, and transmission reliability to establish the asserted group experience. Locked score: The very strong band reflects narrow scope, careful calibration, direct burden relevance, and exceptional responsiveness, with only a limited need to evaluate the residual historical value of inaccessible testimony.

pro-methods-good-ordinary-testimony.words: Extraordinary events need sufficiently reliable evidence, not an exotic evidential category; ordinary eyewitness testimony could suffice if its quality were genuinely strong.
pro-methods-good-ordinary-testimony.critique: Strongest feature: The vivid hypothetical usefully distinguishes an extraordinary event from an extraordinary type of evidence and supports the defensible principle that sufficiently reliable ordinary testimony can establish unusual occurrences. Principal limitation: The example relies on immediate observation and does not answer whether Paul's five-hundred report, apostolic traditions, or other ancient sources possess comparable accessibility, independence, specificity, and reliability across a long transmission distance. Live burden: The affirmative must define evidential strength proportionately and demonstrate that the actual resurrection testimony meets that standard, rather than showing only that ordinary evidence could establish an extraordinary event in principle. Locked score: The mixed band reflects coherent general reasoning, useful conceptual clarification, and meaningful subsidiary relevance, offset by unstable terminology, incomplete application, and failure to resolve the concrete source-access objection.

con-event-acceptance-not-causal-verdict.words: Accepting that an extraordinary return from death occurred would not independently justify a supernatural explanation without separate evidence establishing the relevant causal connection.
con-event-acceptance-not-causal-verdict.critique: Strongest feature: The move draws an exceptionally clear distinction between accepting an extraordinary event and accepting a proposed causal explanation, while explicitly conceding the hypothetical occurrence rather than dismissing it through prior naturalistic commitment. Principal limitation: Event characteristics can sometimes provide causal evidence, so complete separation would be excessive if the observed pattern included independently specified features discriminating among natural, supernatural, intentional, and accidental hypotheses. Live burden: The skeptical side must explain what additional evidence could connect an accepted event to a supernatural cause and show why mere law-transcendence or postmortem return would not independently identify that cause. Locked score: The very strong band reflects outstanding coherence, precision, calibration, charity, and direct responsiveness to the decisive inference, with only a limited need to clarify how event evidence may constrain causes.

pro-causation-event-before-agent.words: An event verified as impossible under natural laws may be called supernatural before identifying whether God, another agent, or something else caused it.
pro-causation-event-before-agent.critique: Strongest feature: The reply carefully limits its conclusion to classifying an event after verified natural impossibility and openly concedes uncertainty about whether God, an angel, another agent, or something else caused it. Principal limitation: It assumes the decisive antecedent without providing a workable historical method for proving incompatibility with natural laws, and its examples blur nonnatural agency, extraterrestrial agency, and the definition of supernatural transcendence. Live burden: The affirmative must distinguish impossibility from current explanatory failure, specify how a singular ancient event could satisfy that demanding standard, and explain what evidential value the resulting classification adds. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects logical clarity, important central relevance, explicit qualification, and charitable acknowledgment of agent uncertainty, tempered by incomplete verification and unstable causal terminology.

pro-background-resurrection-supports-the.words: Resurrection evidence could update belief toward supernaturalism and probably theism without prior proof of God, especially when combined with independent background arguments.
pro-background-resurrection-supports-the.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly rejects an absolute prior-proof requirement and recognizes that event evidence may update background beliefs about supernaturalism or theism rather than operating only after those beliefs are independently established. Principal limitation: The claim that resurrection probably yields God lacks a discriminating bridge from an unusual postmortem event to classical theism, while design, cosmological, and biological considerations are listed without developed supporting argument. Live burden: The affirmative must compare how strongly the event is expected under theism and relevant alternatives, separate generic supernaturalism from purposeful divine action, and justify any cumulative contribution from independent background evidence. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a coherent probabilistic insight and direct contact with the prior-support objection, offset by materially overstated warrant, conceptual instability, and an incomplete agent-identification inference.

strengths: Established an early Pauline and apostolic evidential foundation that directly addressed the historical-appearance burden.
Used explicit explanatory criteria rather than relying solely on the failure of a single naturalistic alternative.
Correctly argued that disciplinary investigation need not require laboratory repeatability and that event classification can be separated from precise agent identification.
Acknowledged qualifications, including uncertainty about the particular cause of a purportedly law-transcending event.

blunders.text: The affirmative repeatedly moved from unresolved phenomena or comparative weaknesses to supernaturalism, resurrection, or probable theism without supplying sufficiently discriminating causal bridges.

strengths: Consistently separated evidence that an event occurred from evidence identifying its cause.
Directly challenged the accessibility and independence of the Pauline, apostolic, and five-hundred appearance reports.
Explained why eliminating fraud or naturalistic rivals does not automatically provide resurrection with positive explanatory content.
Maintained a calibrated withholding position that generally avoided claiming the reported events were disproved.

blunders.text: Several formulations made the skeptical threshold too absolute, especially treating prior belief in a divine agent or positive supernatural ontology as necessary before evidential updating could occur.

premises.text: Resurrection should be compared with strengthened psychological, legendary, fraudulent, mixed, and unknown-cause hypotheses under identical criteria rather than against a narrow hallucination model alone.

novelty.explanation: It repairs incomplete rival coverage and requires symmetrical comparative standards across the full hypothesis set.

premises.text: A supernatural classification is warranted only if the evidence supports more than current explanatory failure and exhibits features that discriminate against relevant known and unknown-cause alternatives.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the gap between excluding methodological dogmatism and positively supporting a supernatural event classification.

premises.text: Evidence for an event may update the probability of purposeful agency, but the magnitude of that update depends on how much more expected the evidence is under theism than under competitors.

novelty.explanation: It replaces an asserted move toward probable theism with an explicitly comparative and proportionate updating rule.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, resurrection may be considered a serious historical hypothesis if its refined evidence set and strengthened comparative analysis outperform relevant alternatives, though that result would not by itself identify classical theism with certainty.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual signature test
newArguments.text: Before examining disputed reports, specify what evidential pattern would be comparatively more expected if a purposeful resurrection occurred: independently transmitted appearances to differently situated witnesses, durable transformation not explained by prior expectation alone, and early public claims tied to a particular person and time. Then ask whether the surviving evidence approximates that signature better than strengthened rivals do. This approach does not infer supernatural causation merely from mystery; it seeks positive contrasts capable of making the hypothesis evidentially distinctive.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a preregistered counterfactual-signature method absent from the transcript moves and avoids reasoning solely from failed alternatives.

newArguments.title: Hierarchical evidence model
newArguments.text: Treat source reliability, event occurrence, event classification, and agent identification as separate inferential layers. Evidence may strongly support an early sincere appearance report while only weakly supporting bodily return, and evidence for bodily return may still weakly identify a divine agent. Updating each layer separately prevents stronger conclusions from inheriting confidence automatically from weaker ones. The affirmative case improves if it shows transparent cumulative gains at every transition and explicitly reports where uncertainty remains instead of compressing all layers into one resurrection verdict.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a layered evidential architecture that separates historical reporting, event inference, causal classification, and agent attribution.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that withholding belief in resurrection remains justified when source limitations, causal underdetermination, and insufficiently discriminating supernatural content prevent the available evidence from establishing either the event or its proposed cause.

novelty.explanation: It extends the skeptical case by integrating source sufficiency, event inference, and causal attribution into one proportionate withholding thesis.

premises.text: The evidential default should be suspension rather than an assumption that resurrection is false, leaving room for updating whenever sufficiently strong and discriminating evidence appears.

novelty.explanation: It repairs unstable null-hypothesis language by defining the default as withholding rather than treating skepticism as true.

premises.text: Ancient testimony deserves weight according to access, independence, specificity, transmission, and corroboration, but the reported five-hundred appearance lacks enough accessible detail for robust investigation.

novelty.explanation: It extends the source criticism while acknowledging that historical testimony can possess degrees of evidential value.

premises.text: Accepting an anomalous or extraordinary event does not automatically identify its cause, although distinctive event features may constrain causal hypotheses when explicit comparative predictions are available.

novelty.explanation: It preserves the event-cause distinction while allowing event evidence to influence causal comparison when genuinely discriminating.

premises.text: A supernatural hypothesis needs operational contrasts showing why the evidence is more expected under that hypothesis than under error, fraud, psychology, transmission effects, or unknown natural causes.

novelty.explanation: It develops the demand for causal discrimination into a comparative evidential standard rather than an absolute ontological prerequisite.

conclusion.text: Therefore, the available case warrants continued investigation and graded confidence in particular historical reports, but not assent to resurrection or divine causation until evidence supplies stronger source support and causal discrimination.

novelty.explanation: It extends the skeptical route into a proportionate conclusion that permits partial historical confidence while withholding the stronger causal verdict.

newArguments.title: Inference-layer error propagation
newArguments.text: Historical reasoning becomes fragile when uncertainty at several stages is collapsed into a single conclusion. Uncertainty about what a source originally claimed combines with uncertainty about witness experience, event occurrence, bodily continuity, causal classification, and agent intention. Even moderately favorable judgments at individual stages can yield a substantially weaker final inference when every stage is required. The skeptical position can therefore grant meaningful evidence at early layers while arguing that the cumulative chain does not yet support resurrection or divine action at the final layer.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an error-propagation argument based on multiple dependent inferential stages rather than any single transcript objection.

newArguments.title: Symmetrical anomaly ledger
newArguments.text: Apply the same evidential ledger to modern paranormal reports and ancient resurrection traditions: provenance, observer access, independence, contemporaneous documentation, opportunity for adversarial checking, and predictions distinguishing candidate causes. This avoids dismissing anomalies merely because they are unusual while preventing poorly documented cases from acquiring strength through repetition alone. If the resurrection evidence performs better than ordinary anomaly reports, that difference should be recorded; if it does not, the comparison supplies a principled reason to withhold causal attribution without presuming naturalism.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a symmetrical cross-domain evidence ledger that tests ancient and modern anomaly claims under identical standards.
